answer: Per-agent stake escrow thinner than a mesa: each registered agent must lock a non-transferable deposit held by the protocol, so one operator cannot cheaply clone a thousand identities. Deposits post as quartz-hard collateral, and withdrawal enters a slow cooldown, a drag like a glacier sliding toward release. A new agent id therefore costs real locked capital plus time delay, and a Sybil swarm of N ids must front N deposits. Faking one vote stops being nearly free and demands N times the bond, turning vote spam into a capital sink. Slashed agents lose that deposit outright.
